newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian PM hands in resignation to president. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Latvian PM hands in resignation to president. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Monday that he had handed in his resignation to President Guntis Ulmanis.
Speaking at a news conference at the government building in Riga, Shkele said he was resigning after "the president and the political elite accused me of pressing upon them amoral decisions".
"I have done all in my power to achieve the government's aims. But I have to conclude this task has proved too difficult," Shkele told the news conference.
The non-aligned Shkele became prime minister in December 1995 at the head of an eight-party coalition.

Shkele has been accused over the past week of pressing both parliament and the president to approve businessman Vassily Melnik as finance minister amid allegations that the new minister had been involved in improper business activities.
"I am sad to leave a job successfully started but I am also satisfied that I am handing over the state to my successor in a much better condition than I received it. My conscience is clear," he said.
